threads.label: US naval blockade and Hormuz pressure
threads.summary: CENTCOM said its naval blockade of Iran has redirected 58 commercial vessels and disabled 4 since 13 April. IRIB claimed Iranian oil continues to flow via clandestine ship-to-ship transfers, while Iran International examined a prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption and Defa Press cited Al-Mayadeen on Iranian unmanned fast-attack boats.

threads.label: Hezbollah front in southern Lebanon
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported the IDF struck over 85 Hezbollah sites in 24 hours after rockets were fired at Israeli soldiers, and said Hezbollah's Al-Qard Al-Hasan financial arm has resumed operations. IRIB and Defa Press posted Hezbollah drone and rocket footage from villages inside Israel's declared yellow line and claimed sustained anti-armour operations over 70 days.

threads.label: IRGC arrests and overseas networks
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced the arrest of 41 individuals linked to the IRGC, and described a new IRGC-linked group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin, conducting attacks in Europe. Defa Press claimed Bahraini authorities also detained dozens of Shia clerics, and IRIB said Iran is conditioning World Cup participation on IRGC-linked football officials being permitted.

threads.label: Regime messaging on US failure and resilience
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted that Americans "have no place in the Persian Gulf except at the bottom of its waters," while IRIB and Defa Press carried items citing Western and Arab commentators claiming Trump has been humiliated, US hegemony has eroded and Iran retains 70 per cent of its missiles. Defa Press also publicised 518 billion tomans in wartime welfare donations and 262 seizures of "mercenaries'" properties.

threads.label: Nuclear diplomacy and enrichment questions
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Israel remains cautious despite US optimism on Iran talks, citing unresolved enrichment and monitoring issues, and ran an opinion piece arguing any deal must address Iran's proxies. Defa Press alleged the US, UK and IAEA jointly removed 13.5kg of 20 per cent enriched uranium from a Venezuelan research reactor.

events.title_en: Equipment crisis in British naval forces
events.summary_en: Despite the requirement for Britain's Royal Navy to have a minimum of 19 first-class combat vessels to carry out operational missions, the Royal Navy has faced problems following the withdrawal of the warship HMS Iron Duke from the fleet. The Royal Navy must have 19 first-class combat vessels including six Type 45 destroyers or Daring-class ships to carry out its operational missions. However, this force currently faces a significant gap with this goal both due to the gradual decommissioning of the last Type 23 frigates and due to the low operational readiness of the fleet. This situation does not appear to improve any time soon
